limits: Both packages are development snapshots; no independently released-package compatibility is claimed.
Acceptance is bound to these gen11/gen16-async installed seals, complete JavaScript graphs and native bytes; later source or package changes require separate acceptance.
Package versions and revision-like labels do not establish immutable source-commit provenance; recorded hashes identify the observed implementations.
Windows SendInput was used, not human physical-key evidence.
This lane is x64 D3D11 Gun Frog at observed DPI96/DPR1; x86 package integrity is not x86 game acceptance, and fractional or multiple DPI configurations were not measured.
OS module snapshots plus module-file hashes identify observed modules, not remote-memory bytes or a historical count of every injection or initialization attempt.
Retired add-on code remained mapped in the original game; scene retirement and survivor rendering/input establish participant isolation. Only the fresh relaunch excludes the retired add-on.
Crash cells force-killed an Electron producer; they do not inject an unhandled native fault or establish fault containment among modules in the shared game process.
Initial late-member authentication is retained in target-authenticated events and controller assertions; final survivor states contain the relaunched target identity.
Embedded finalStates and standalone raw states represent different capture times; raw files can include later cleanup disconnect/exit updates.
This record does not certify the complete feature/backend or original-game/manual-key matrix.
Raw build artifacts preserve original absolute paths; this portable audit uses repository-relative artifact paths and exact raw-file hashes.

roles: independent full installed-payload and PE audit
